When C.A. Bradley, of Huddersfield, entered for the A.A.A. 100 Yards Championship at Northampton in 1893, he was informed before the race that as the track was a shade downhill, and the wind was blowing in the same direction, if he made a record under those circumstances it would probably not be passed by the A.A.A.
Lawton, having warmed up in the Southern '20' gave it warp factor five over the toughest 50k in the country; and having led for 21 miles had the race snatched from him by Colin Bradley of Trowbridge.
